bullets: The new Two-Stage Measurement of Update Adherence benchmark tests whether a memory-enabled language-model agent follows a revised requirement rather than the requirement it replaced. It scores both the context assembled by the memory system and the agent’s final answer using deterministic rules, without another language model acting as judge. Why it matters: If you are evaluating agent memory, this design separates retrieval failures from answer-generation failures instead of collapsing them into one score. That distinction can determine whether to change the memory engine, the answering model, or both, while deterministic scoring makes repeated comparisons easier to reproduce. Evidence: E021. High confidence.

The new SimGlot Frozen Evaluation Dataset packages four frozen evaluation configurations and their supporting evidence from a study of oracle failures and configuration-dependent measurement in an agent benchmark. An oracle is the component that decides whether an agent’s result counts as correct. Why it matters: If you are relying on an agent benchmark for model selection, this archive provides a way to test whether reported measurements survive changes in evaluator configuration and to reproduce the original runs from fixed inputs. It makes the evaluator itself an inspectable part of the measurement rather than an assumed source of truth. Evidence: E001. High confidence.

The new Tariff Cost Benchmark evaluates customs classification on 228 binding rulings issued after the latest training cutoff among the compared models, while reporting all 1,098 rulings separately as an upper-bound analysis. It also frames errors by the customs duty at stake rather than treating every wrong tariff code as equally consequential. Why it matters: If you are comparing models for customs work, the post-cutoff subset reduces the risk that memorized rulings drive the ranking, and duty-weighted analysis connects classification errors to financial exposure. That can change model selection when two systems have similar accuracy but make mistakes with different cost consequences. Evidence: E038. High confidence.

The new NetFlow intrusion-detection audit releases code, result files, and partition checksums for record-level checks across several benchmark versions, plus in-domain, cross-dataset, replication, and feature-attribution experiments. The underlying datasets are not included. Why it matters: If you are choosing an intrusion-detection benchmark, the artifact supports checking whether duplicate records, partition choices, or dataset-specific shortcuts affect measured performance. Cross-dataset evaluation can reveal when a detector succeeds on one benchmark’s peculiarities rather than transferring to another captured network dataset. Evidence: E002. Medium confidence.

The new Search Anything benchmark provides a frozen multimodal retrieval set with 1,150 candidate assets and 350 text queries sampled from seven existing datasets, together with preparation scripts, a search pipeline, and an evaluation runner. Its compact size is intended for repeated local regression checks with limited storage. Why it matters: If you are testing changes to a search system that retrieves across different media, this offers a lightweight, fixed target for catching regressions before running larger suites. Its value is operational comparability and local iteration speed, not evidence that performance will generalize beyond the sampled assets and queries. Evidence: E003. High confidence.

The new Agent Overspend Benchmark tests purchasing agents on 20 pushy-user requests covering five rule-evasion tactics, with repeated trials against two agent setups in a test-money sandbox. The publisher discloses that its own sandbox is also the system under test. Why it matters: If you are evaluating an agent that can spend money, this introduces scenarios aimed at whether user pressure can bypass purchasing constraints, rather than measuring task completion alone. The small scenario set and publisher involvement limit comparative claims, but the design can inform whether a product test plan includes overspending and policy-evasion failures. Evidence: E008. Medium confidence.
bullets_zh: 新的 Two-Stage Measurement of Update Adherence 基准测试启用了记忆的语言模型智能体是否遵循修订后的要求，而不是该要求所取代的旧要求。它使用确定性规则，分别对记忆系统组装的上下文和智能体的最终答案进行评分，无需由另一个语言模型充当评判者。Why it matters: 如果你正在评估智能体记忆，这种设计可将检索失败与答案生成失败区分开来，而不是将二者合并为一个分数。这一区分可以决定应更换记忆引擎、作答模型，还是两者都更换；同时，确定性评分也使重复比较更易于复现。Evidence: E021. High confidence.

新的 SimGlot Frozen Evaluation Dataset 打包了四套冻结的评估配置及其支持证据，这些内容来自一项针对智能体基准中判定器失效和依赖配置的测量问题的研究。判定器是决定智能体结果是否算作正确的组件。Why it matters: 如果你依赖智能体基准来选择模型，该档案提供了一种方法，可测试报告的测量结果在评估器配置发生变化后是否仍然成立，并使用固定输入复现原始运行。它使评估器本身成为测量中可供检查的一部分，而不再被视为理所当然的事实来源。Evidence: E001. High confidence.

新的 Tariff Cost Benchmark 使用在参评模型最新训练截止日期之后发布的 228 项具有约束力的裁定来评估海关归类，同时另行报告全部 1,098 项裁定，作为上限分析。它还根据所涉及的关税来衡量错误，而不是认为每个错误的税则编码后果都相同。Why it matters: 如果你正在比较用于海关业务的模型，截止日期后的子集可降低模型排名由记忆中的裁定所驱动的风险，而按关税加权的分析则将归类错误与财务风险敞口联系起来。当两个系统的准确率相近，但所犯错误带来的成本后果不同时，这可能改变模型选择。Evidence: E038. High confidence.

新的 NetFlow 入侵检测审计发布了代码、结果文件以及跨多个基准版本进行记录级检查所需的分区校验和，此外还包括域内、跨数据集、复现和特征归因实验。底层数据集未包含在内。Why it matters: 如果你正在选择入侵检测基准，该工件可用于检查重复记录、分区选择或数据集特有的捷径是否会影响测得的性能。跨数据集评估可以揭示检测器究竟只是利用了某个基准的特殊性，还是能够迁移到另一个采集的网络数据集。Evidence: E002. Medium confidence.

新的 Search Anything 基准提供了一个冻结的多模态检索集，其中包含从七个现有数据集抽样得到的 1,150 个候选资产和 350 个文本查询，并附有准备脚本、搜索流水线和评估运行器。其紧凑规模旨在支持存储空间有限条件下的重复本地回归检查。Why it matters: 如果你正在测试跨不同媒体进行检索的搜索系统变更，该基准可提供一个轻量、固定的目标，以便在运行更大规模的测试套件之前发现回归问题。它的价值在于操作层面的可比性和本地迭代速度，而不是证明性能能够泛化到抽样资产和查询之外。Evidence: E003. High confidence.

新的 Agent Overspend Benchmark 使用涵盖五种规避规则策略的 20 项强势用户请求来测试采购智能体，并在测试资金沙盒中针对两种智能体配置进行重复试验。发布方披露，其自有沙盒同时也是受测系统。Why it matters: 如果你正在评估能够花钱的智能体，该基准引入了一些场景，旨在测试用户施压能否绕过采购约束，而不只是衡量任务完成情况。场景集规模较小且发布方参与其中，这限制了比较性结论，但这种设计有助于判断产品测试计划是否涵盖超支和规避政策类故障。Evidence: E008. Medium confidence.

evidence_items.summary: This dataset provides frozen aggregate evaluation results from a study comparing four sensory-attribute extraction systems—Lexicon, Embedding, Local LLM, and API LLM—on consumer reviews of tea products from Amazon Reviews'23. The evaluation uses a hierarchical sensory ontology comprising 7 broad sensory dimensions (L1) and 35 specific sensory attributes (L2). Results are reported separately for a representative held-out test set of 600 sentences and an enriched challenge test set of 200 sentences. The archive contains 336 class-level performance records, 16 overall evaluation summaries, eight prespecified paired comparisons, selected diagnostic results, frozen method configurations, and a Python script for verifying aggregate evaluation metrics. The dataset supports verification of reported aggregate performance estimates. It does not contain original consumer review text, user identifiers, sentence-level human annotations, or sentence-level model predictions. The provided verification script does not independently reproduce model inference or bootstrap confidence intervals. Original data source: Amazon Reviews'23, Grocery and Gourmet Food category, McAuley Lab (https://amazon-reviews-2023.github.io/).
evidence_items.title: Hierarchical Sensory-Attribute Extraction from Tea Reviews: Frozen Aggregate Evaluation Dataset

evidence_items.summary: Long-context audio reasoning is underserved in both training data and evaluation. Existing benchmarks target short-context tasks, and the open-ended generation tasks most relevant to long-context reasoning pose well-known challenges for automatic evaluation. We propose a synthetic data generation pipeline designed to serve both as a training resource and as a controlled evaluation environment, and instantiate it for first-visit doctor-patient conversations with SOAP note generation as the task. The pipeline has three stages, persona-driven dialogue generation, multi-speaker audio synthesis with overlap/pause modeling, room acoustics, and sound events, and LLM-based reference SOAP note production, built entirely on open-weight models. We release 8,800 synthetic conversations with 1.3k hours of corresponding audio and reference notes. Evaluating current open-weight systems, we find that cascaded approaches still substantially outperform end-to-end models.
evidence_items.title: Generating Synthetic Doctor-Patient Conversations for Long-form Audio Summarization

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Sixth generation (6G) networks require intelligent and privacy-preserving solutions to handle traffic complexity, resource allocation, and security challenges. While Large Language Models (LLMs) offer advanced reasoning and Federated Artificial Intelligence (FAI) enables distributed learning without directly sharing raw data, their combined application in large-scale network science remains limited. Key issues include non-IID data, decision latency, and limited robustness of centralized models. To address these challenges, this work introduces FALCON-6G (Federated AI and LLM-Oriented Cognitive Optimization in 6G Networks), a novel framework for distributed anomaly detection, traffic prediction, and adaptive resource management. Experiments conducted under federated learning settings with 50 participating clients and 200 global communication rounds on two Open RAN and four intrusion detection datasets show a 22.7% average relative improvement in throughput prediction accuracy and a 17.6% reduction in decision latency compared with FedAvg, along with up to a 23.9% relative improvement in intrusion detection F1-score over FedAvg and a 34.0% reduction in communication overhead. These results demonstrate the potential of FALCON-6G for privacy-aware 6G network optimization. The current evaluation is primarily based on benchmark datasets, and validation in live large-scale 6G/O-RAN environments remains an important direction for future work.
evidence_items.title: Enhancing network science with large language models and federated artificial intelligence

evidence_items.summary: Tersoff-NN is a hybrid machine-learned interatomic potential for silicon that retains the analytical radial interactions and cutoff structure of the Tersoff potential while representing its environment-dependent bond-order factor using compact neural networks. This archive provides the DFT reference dataset comprising 16,874 silicon configurations, training codes and trained models for three bond-order neural network architectures, and LAMMPS implementations and input files for molecular dynamics simulations. The three architectures are ACSF-BOPNN, triplet fixed-map BOPNN, and triplet learned-map BOPNN, the last of which corresponds to Tersoff-NN. The archive also contains benchmark logs and supporting files used to evaluate computational efficiency and dynamical stability. These materials are provided to support reproducibility of the results reported in the accompanying manuscript by Yusuke Nishimura, Sho Kubota, Kotaro Takematsu, Kentaro Hirai, and Takanobu Watanabe. Please refer to the included README files for information on the dataset, software dependencies, model parameters, and simulation procedures.

evidence_items.summary: Machine Reading Comprehension (MRC) has become a key benchmark for evaluating natural language processing systems, and multiple-choice question answering is widely adopted for assessing reasoning, comprehension, and commonsense inference capabilities. However, traditional embedding-based approaches often struggle with complex reasoning and have limited access to external knowledge. Although Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong language understanding and reasoning abilities, relying on a single model remains challenging because of hallucinations, model biases, and differences in training data, architectures, and domain expertise. Consequently, no single model consistently performs best across diverse multiple-choice question answering tasks. To address these limitations, we propose an ensemble framework for multiple-choice question answering. The framework incorporates a model selection mechanism that identifies model combinations with complementary error patterns to improve the error-correction capability of the ensemble. In addition, when disagreements occur among the selected base models, a Thinking Model is dynamically invoked to resolve conflicting predictions, thereby reserving advanced reasoning for cases requiring additional resolution. We evaluate nine open-source LLMs on five datasets in Chinese and English. Each dataset is partitioned into 30% validation data for model selection and 70% held-out test data for final evaluation, with the experiment independently repeated five times. Experimental results show that the proposed framework outperforms the individual LLMs on five datasets and achieves an average error-rate reduction ranging from 3.46% to 7.14% relative to conventional ensemble baselines. Furthermore, the proposed approach reduces the average number of Thinking Model invocations by 87.83% compared with the strongest benchmark model while maintaining comparable accuracy, demonstrating a favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-off.
evidence_items.title: Ensemble Voting of Large Language Models for Multiple-Choice Answer Prediction

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Background This study aimed to develop and externally validate an instruction-tuned multimodal large language model (MLLM) for early warning and early diagnosis of dry eye disease (DED) using routinely obtainable clinical data. Methods A total of 874 participants were enrolled, including an internal development cohort (n = 743) from Peking University Third Hospital (October 2024 to August 2025) and an independent external validation cohort (n = 131) from three additional centers. Participants included both DED and non-DED individuals, diagnosed according to the Chinese Expert Consensus (2020) and TFOS DEWS II criteria. We developed DED-MLLM on the basis of Qwen2-VL and constructed a domain-specific instruction-tuning dataset integrating Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI), Standard Patient Evaluation of Eye Dryness (SPEED), self-reported questionnaires, ophthalmic imaging, and clinical examination data. Model performance was evaluated for risk stratification and diagnosis under both diagnostic frameworks, with ablation analyses used to examine the relative contributions of visual and structured clinical modalities. Results Based on the international diagnostic criteria for DED, the model achieved an accuracy of 0.8232 for early warning (specificity: 0.6873, sensitivity: 0.9558) and an accuracy of 0.9203 for diagnosis (specificity: 0.8776, sensitivity: 0.9720). According to the Chinese diagnostic criteria for DED, the model achieved an accuracy of 0.9584 for early warning (specificity: 0.9112, sensitivity: 0.9927) and an accuracy of 0.9327 for diagnosis (specificity: 0.8742, sensitivity: 0.9851). External validation showed AUCs of 0.910 and 0.957 for early warning and 0.960 and 0.893 for diagnosis. Ablation analyses indicated that structured clinical information contributed most strongly to diagnostic performance, whereas image-based information provided complementary, interpretable ocular-surface evidence.
evidence_items.title: Development of a Multimodal Large Language Model for Early Warning and Diagnosis of Dry Eye Disease

evidence_items.summary: Conventional in-situ monitoring solutions—such as high-speed cameras, SWIR imaging, and acoustic emission sensors—are costly, data-intensive, and impractical for industrial deployment. In this work, we demonstrate a low-cost, off-the-shelf ultrasonic microphone installed inside the build chamber as a practical alternative for capturing high-resolution acoustic signals during LPBF. Using these signals, we benchmark multiple machine learning architectures for localized porosity prediction. Targets for lack-of-fusion and keyhole porosity are derived from volumetric X-ray Computed Tomography (XCT) analysis and carefully registered to process coordinates, enabling supervised learning at scanline granularity. Beyond performance evaluation, we conduct explainability analysis using feature attribution methods to uncover which acoustic signatures most strongly correlate with defect formation. Results show that acoustic-based models achieve low-latency inference, suitable for in-process monitoring, paving the way for adaptive corrective control strategies. This study establishes a new paradigm for practical, scalable LPBF quality assurance by combining low-cost sensing with interpretable AI.
evidence_items.title: Sound Of Porosity: Unlocking Local Acoustic Signatures Of Porosity In LPBF Via Low-Cost Sensing And Explainable AI

evidence_items.summary: Building robust IMU-based human activity recognition (HAR) systems requires tuning the full sensing pipeline, not only the model. We present AutoResearcHAR, a multi-agent framework for dataset-adaptive HAR optimization. A Data Agent refines source selection, preprocessing, windowing, and sampling; a Model Agent improves architecture and training choices; and an Augmentation Agent designs IMU augmentation and synthetic-data strategies. An Orchestrator composes compatible proposals, while an LLM-based Judge filters candidate edits before empirical evaluation. The system performs iterative hill climbing over bounded code and configuration level changes, retaining candidates that improve Macro-F1. We evaluate AutoResearcHAR on 10 IMU-HAR datasets using leave-one-subject-out evaluation and 3 held out datasets using leave-one-dataset-out evaluation. AutoResearcHAR improves over the best non-agent baselines by 1.2 to 12.9 Macro-F1 points in LOSO and 2.3 to 8.9 points in LODO, showing the value of coordinated multi-agent pipeline search for wearable sensing.
evidence_items.title: AutoResearcHAR: A Multi-Agent Framework for Dataset Adaptive IMU Based Human Activity Recognition

evidence_items.summary: Decision trees built with greedy axis-aligned splits perform well when individual features carry a meaningful signal about the target. They fail, often badly, in the setting where the useful information resides in the joint behaviour of two or more features rather than in any single one. The exclusive-or problem is the textbook example, since no single feature predicts the label but the pair does. This study presents SCMI-Tree, a tree induction algorithm whose splitting score augments mutual information with two additional terms, namely a synergy bonus for features that interact constructively with the ancestor splits along the path, and a redundancy penalty for features that overlap with them. A dataset-level synergy score is computed once at fit time from a random sample of feature pairs, which allows the algorithm to decide whether to engage a lookahead mechanism that addresses the root exclusive-or problem, and to skip that overhead when it would not help. SCMI-Tree was evaluated on eight classification datasets comprising four real benchmarks and four synthetic tasks of varying difficulty. The lookahead variant achieved the best average rank of 1.88 across the eight datasets, outperforming both Gini-based CART at 4.12 and entropy-based ID3 at 2.75. On a noisy exclusive-or task with eight irrelevant features the difference was substantial, reaching 89.3% accuracy for SCMI-Tree against 53.2% for CART. Ablation experiments show that two failure modes of conventional greedy induction, namely sensitivity to noise features and dependence on tree depth, are largely avoided by the proposed method
evidence_items.title: SCMI-TREE: SYNERGY-AWARE DECISION TREES VIA CONDITIONAL MUTUAL INFORMATION WITH ADAPTIVE LOOKAHEAD

evidence_items.summary: The success of generative molecular design depends on the synthetic accessibility of the molecules it creates. While computational models can help predict chemical reactions, their current effectiveness is limited by a lack of reference data and the difficulty of accurately predicting reaction regioselectivity. Here, to address this, we present an integrated closed-loop workflow that combines efficient reaction data acquisition with high-accuracy deep learning. We developed an active learning strategy, driven by a tree-based ensemble, to guide the acquisition of the most informative laboratory experiments. This experimental campaign yielded a diverse benchmark for C-H borylation. The bespoke dataset allowed us to train and evaluate geometric graph neural networks. We demonstrate that augmenting these symmetry-aware models with self-supervised auxiliary tasks consistently improves performance for both reaction outcome prediction and regioselectivity prediction. Prospective tests on unseen substrates, featuring challenging N-heteroaryl motifs, pinpointed the correct borylation positions in all cases, illustrating the practical utility of our workflow for efficient drug optimization.
evidence_items.title: Advancing chemical reaction prediction in data-scarce drug discovery with active and geometric deep learning.

evidence_items.summary: Bitcoin’s price follows a well-documented power law over long time scales, yet this trend alone is a poor short-term predictor: at horizons of a few months, today’s price outperforms any trend extrapolation. We construct a deliberately minimal baseline, the Naive–Power Law blend (NvPL), which interpolates smoothly from today’s price (at short horizons) to the fitted power-law trend (at long horizons), and ask whether more elaborate models can beat it out of sample. We compare a broad set of alternatives: mean-reversion and momentum corrections, shrinkage regressions (ridge, LASSO, and elastic net), tree-based machine learning (gradient boosting and random forests), and 18 Bayesian structural time series specifications, some hand-specified and some discovered by an autonomous AI agent (the autoresearch pattern). Every model is evaluated on five non-overlapping two-year periods spanning distinct market conditions (2016–2026). For every primary benchmark candidate—the blend and the shrinkage and tree learners—all tunable settings, including the baseline’s own, are selected on training data alone; the Bayesian specifications are deliberately granted more information as a diagnostic. None reliably improves on NvPL. Formal forecast-comparison tests (Diebold–Mariano, Clark–West, and the Model Confidence Set, with inference that treats the forecast origin as the observational unit) sharpen the picture for the primary candidates: no correction significantly improves on NvPL, and the confidence set retains NvPL while excluding the pure power law. The blend’s structure carries detectable predictive content over a pure no-change forecast (Clark–West), but strictly out of sample this content is too small to reliably separate the two in realized error at one to six months: persistence dominates, and the naive forecast is not excluded from the pooled confidence set. Return-based metrics agree, and no model demonstrates directional accuracy above the always-up rule once forecast dependence is accounted for. Aggressive in-sample tuning, including the agent’s, reverses sharply out of sample, illustrating how greedy search overfits non-stationary financial data. At one to six months, short-term Bitcoin prices are dominated by persistence, and NvPL is a stringent, reproducible benchmark that more complex models should be required to beat.
evidence_items.title: The naive–power law blend as a robust baseline for bitcoin price forecasting

evidence_items.summary: This study examines whether explainable machine-learning approaches can support more inclusive credit scoring while maintaining acceptable predictive performance, transparency, and fairness in an emerging-market microfinance setting. We analyzed a de-identified dataset of 2500 resolved loan applications obtained from participating microfinance institutions in the MENA region during 2022–2023. Nine supervised algorithms were compared, spanning classical benchmarks (Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, Support Vector Machine, K-Nearest Neighbors) and modern gradient-boosting frameworks (XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost). Default (90 + days past due) was modeled as the positive class. Performance was evaluated on a held-out test set using ROC-AUC and PR-AUC with bootstrap confidence intervals, supported by repeated stratified cross-validation and DeLong tests. Interpretability was assessed with SHAP, including stability and cross-model consistency checks, and fairness was evaluated using disparate impact, equal opportunity, predictive parity, group-level calibration, and intersectional analysis. An ablation design isolated the incremental contribution of non-traditional indicators. CatBoost achieved the highest test-set discrimination (ROC-AUC = 0.783, 95% CI [0.741, 0.825]; PR-AUC = 0.506) but was statistically indistinguishable from regularized Logistic Regression (ROC-AUC = 0.780; DeLong p = .59), and no gradient-boosting model significantly outperformed the logistic benchmark. SHAP analysis identified Credit Score Category, Utility Payment Behavior, and Repayment History as the dominant predictors, with rankings highly stable under resampling (Spearman ρ = 0.999) and consistent across model families (ρ = 0.95–0.98 among tree ensembles). Adding non-traditional indicators produced a positive but statistically non-significant incremental gain (ΔAUC = + 0.008, 95% CI [− 0.010, 0.027]). Disparate impact ratios exceeded the 0.80 heuristic for Gender (0.956), Geographic Region (0.961), and all gender-by-region intersections (0.881), with small equal-opportunity and predictive-parity gaps, although rural applicants experienced a higher false-positive rate than urban applicants (0.680 vs. 0.492). In this microfinance context, transparent and well-calibrated models matched the discrimination of complex ensembles, non-traditional indicators carried weak evidence of incremental predictive value despite meaningful within-model signal but limited incremental discrimination, and headline parity metrics coexisted with subgroup error-rate asymmetries. These findings support explainability- and governance-centered model selection for inclusive credit scoring, while underscoring the need for multi-metric fairness auditing, external validation, and continued monitoring in operational deployment.
evidence_items.title: Explainable machine learning models for AI enabled credit scoring and financial inclusion in emerging markets

evidence_items.summary: Abstract. This dataset documents a 90-day independent benchmark of 14 IPTV service providers operating in the United States market during Q3-Q4 2026. The study measured stream stability during live sports events, channel availability across US broadcast and cable networks (NFL, NBA, MLB, UFC), device compatibility across six major streaming platforms, refund-UX processing times, and price-to-feature ratios for the best IPTV USA 2026 market. Research question. Which IPTV service provider delivers the most consistent live-event performance for United States cord-cutters at the lowest total cost of ownership in 2026? Methodology. Residential IP testing was conducted across four United States cities: Columbus (Ohio) on AT&T Fiber 1 Gbps, Austin (Texas) on Spectrum Internet Ultra, Orlando (Florida) on Xfinity Gigabit, and San Jose (California) on Comcast Gigabit. Each provider was evaluated across 13 consecutive weeks on six streaming devices: Fire TV Stick 4K Max, Apple TV 4K, Chromecast with Google TV, Samsung Tizen Smart TV, NVIDIA Shield Pro, and Roku Ultra. Live-event stress windows included NFL Sunday afternoon simulcasts (CBS/FOX), NBA regional feeds, MLB blackout-safe streams, UFC pay-per-view main cards (3 events during the study window), and WWE Premium Live Events. Service providers evaluated. OrvenTV, AireStream Prime, BroadcastHub TV, RedCord IPTV, 4K Ultra Pulse, FlixBridge, GlobeLive One, Nimbus HD, PineStream, Zenith Streams, DigitaLine IPTV, StreamKing, FlexStream, and ClearView IPTV. Measurement criteria. (1) Re-buffer event count during live sports windows, (2) channel-quality consistency verified at 1080p and 4K resolutions, (3) EPG metadata accuracy, (4) setup time from install to first live channel, (5) native streaming device app availability, (6) refund-UX speed via burner-account cancellation test, (7) support response time on game-night tickets, (8) price per concurrent connection. Key findings.

evidence_items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) such as GPT-4 and DeepSeek have shown potential in medical education and assessment. In China, the Chinese National Medical Licensing Examination (CNMLE) has become a critical benchmark for evaluating LLMs’ professional knowledge and reasoning ability in non-English contexts. This scoping review aims to synthesize research evaluating LLM performance on the CNMLE and related Chinese medical examinations, identifying performance trends, methodological gaps, and future directions. A scoping review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines. PubMed and Web of Science were searched on June 12, 2025, using terms related to LLMs and Chinese medical examinations. Studies were included if they evaluated any LLM on national-level Chinese medical exams and reported performance metrics. Two reviewers screened and extracted data. Study quality was assessed using a 12-item checklist covering dataset characteristics, LLM setup, and evaluation methods. Fisher’s exact test was used to assess differences in the passing rates of different LLMs. 14 studies were included, covering 51 evaluation records across 8 types of Chinese medical examinations, including CNMLE and specialty exams such as critical care, radiation oncology, and ultrasound medicine. Exam years ranged from 2017 to 2024, with a shift toward using recent exams. A total of 9 LLMs were evaluated, including GPT-3.5, GPT-4, GPT-4o, ERNIE, DeepSeek-R1, Qwen-72B, Baichuan2-7B, Baichuan2-13B and DISC-MedLLM. GPT-4o and DeepSeek-R1 achieved the highest scores of 552 (92.00%) and 523 (87.20%) in the 2024 CNMLE, respectively, both surpassing the passing threshold. In an exploratory comparison, GPT-4 achieved a higher pass rate than GPT-3.5 with a statistically significant difference, although inconsistencies in datasets, model transparency, and evaluation criteria persist across the included studies. LLMs show improving performance on Chinese medical exams, especially newer models.
evidence_items.title: Performance of large language models in the Chinese National Medical Licensing Examinations and Beyond: Scoping review

evidence_items.summary: Abstract. Ice-nucleating particles (INPs) catalyze primary ice formation, thereby raising the glaciation temperature of mixed-phase clouds. Glaciation substantially alters cloud microphysical and radiative properties. Therefore, the development and validation of models that predict INP concentrations receive considerable attention. Current model validations rely on sparse observational datasets. These validations compare modeled and measured INP concentrations at individual measurement points, but do not consider their temporal variability. This variability reflects the physical processes controlling INP abundance, and it therefore offers a largely unexploited constraint on the model physics. This study presents a multi-campaign dataset consisting of 110 000 immersion-mode INP observations. Statistical adjustments for differing sampling intervals and campaign durations are derived that allow the heterogeneous dataset to be synthesized into a global characterization of INP concentrations. The campaign means of INP concentrations at -23 °C span more than four orders of magnitude, from Antarctica to agricultural continental sites. The within-campaign spread is around half an order of magnitude and increases with temperature. A multi-campaign time-series analysis shows that almost half the variance of daily values resides within a week, and roughly 20 % beyond 3 months. Across the resolved temperatures (-28 to -15 °C), organic material accounts for up to 90 % of the INP population in the sampled environments. Earlier modeling studies that attribute most INPs to mineral dust therefore likely overestimate the dust contribution. The extensive collection of INP observations and the derived statistics of INP variation provide a strong foundation for improved model evaluation.
evidence_items.title: The spatio-temporal variability of ice-nucleating particle concentrations quantified with a new benchmark dataset

evidence_items.summary: Background: Crop recommendation is one of the most critical challenges in precision agriculture, requiring accurate predictions and rigorous evaluation for reliable decisions. However, previous research has employed ad hoc model selection, lack of statistical validation and limited interpretability, thereby limiting reproducibility and scientific credibility. Methods: A statistically rigorous multi-classifier benchmarking framework for crop recommendation is developed. A publicly available dataset was refined to 33,000 agronomically relevant samples from 57,000, covering 33 crop classes and seven features. A novel K-fold selection criterion optimising predictive accuracy, stability and diversity selected K=7. Friedman testing (χ2=59.23, p=1.89×10-9) with Nemenyi post-hoc analysis confirmed statistical significance of inter-model differences. Result: Random Forest was selected as the top-ranked method through a transparent multi-criteria framework. Optuna TPE (50 trials) yielded CV F1=96.63%, Test F1=97.06%, AUC=0.9996 and generalisation gap=0.47%. Humidity and rainfall are consistently dominant predictors in both MDI and SHAP, while potassium has elevated SHAP importance, reinforcing its agronomic relevance. The frame work enhances reliability, transparency and interpretability for data-driven agricultural decision-making.
evidence_items.title: A Statistically Rigorous Multi-classifier Benchmark for Crop Recommendation: K-fold Selection Criterion, Friedman-nemenyi Testing and Optuna TPE Optimisation

evidence_items.summary: Multimodal AI's video comprehension reflects real-world dynamic understanding, but mainstream Video-Language Interaction (Video QA) benchmarks are primarily English-centric, narrow-domain, and only test basic perceptual or reasoning skills, lacking holistic assessment of model performance across diverse languages, domains, and complex spatiotemporal scenarios. To address these gaps, we present VideoVista, a versatile multilingual and multidomain video comprehension benchmark, built via scalable, quality-controlled automatic QA generation and manual refinement. Evaluations on 41 leading MLLMs reveal three key findings: 1) Small 7/8B open-source models rival large commercial ones with Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning; 2) Models perform poorly (accuracy $\lt $63%) on tasks requiring complex temporal reasoning (e.g., Streaming QA), with most open-source models degrading further when key information appears late in videos; 3) Fine-grained tasks (e.g., anomaly detection) see sharp performance drops and models exhibit cultural bias. We release the benchmark, automatic QA generation framework, and associated pretraining, instruction-tuning, and reinforcement learning datasets at https://github.com/HITsz-TMG/VideoVista.
evidence_items.title: VideoVista: Benchmarking Diverse and Complex Video-Language Interaction for MLLMs.

evidence_items.summary: Clinicians routinely make decisions for patients whose comorbidities, prior therapies, laboratory abnormalities, or demographic characteristics are not reflected in the supporting evidence, even though these factors can influence treatment selection. Given this gap in the evidence base, we sought to evaluate how AI models respond to clinical questions in which patient characteristics or the treatment comparison and outcome of interest may affect the applicability of available evidence. We developed and publicly released Precision Evidence Bench, a benchmark of 209 synthetic clinical questions with specified population, intervention, comparator, and outcome (PICO) elements. Each answer is assessed using a five item rubric that evaluates whether a single cited source matches the PICO and whether the answer faithfully reports its sources. The item verdicts determine one of five ratings, ranging from Precision match to Unsupported claim, without requiring a reference answer. We evaluated four frontier large language models (LLMs) using web search across all 209 questions, then repeated the evaluation with additional access to a corpus of precision evidence-based findings (pEBFs) designed to address these evidence gaps, using two corpus sizes. For every model, Precision match rates increased with the amount of precision evidence available, from 13 to 18% with web search alone to 17 to 28% with 100 million pEBFs and 41 to 56% with 500 million pEBFs. These findings suggest that access to matching evidence is an important determinant of LLM performance on precision medicine questions.
evidence_items.title: Precision Evidence Bench: Assessing PICO alignment and faithful reporting in clinical AI

evidence_items.summary:
OBJECTIVE
This study investigates how domain-aligned self-supervised pretraining influences downstream PET/CT tumor segmentation, with a focus on disentangling the roles of domain proximity and pretraining dataset scale. Approach: We compared nnU-Net segmentation models initialized from random weights or from DINOv3 encoders pretrained on natural images, X-ray mammography, CT, or PET, using datasets of different sizes. To disentangle the effects of pretraining domain and dataset size, CT-DINOv3 encoders were pretrained using different numbers of 2D CT slices, including subsets matched in size to the pretraining datasets from other domains. Models were evaluated on two PET/CT benchmarks, autoPET (whole-body, FDG/PSMA) and HECKTOR (head-and-neck primary tumors and metastatic lymph nodes), using five-fold cross-validation with frozen encoders. Main results: CT-pretrained models achieved the highest Dice scores for lymph nodes, FDG lesions, and PSMA lesions. For primary tumors, PET pretraining produced the highest observed Dice score, followed by CT pretraining, suggesting the potential benefit of in-domain representations when PET data are sufficient. Notably, PET pretraining exceeded CT pretraining using equally sized datasets for PSMA but remained below models pretrained on larger CT datasets for both PSMA and FDG targets. In contrast, natural-image pretraining did not outperform from-scratch training despite its much larger pretraining scale, indicating that scale alone is insufficient when domain proximity is low. Across comparisons, strong transfer reflected the combination of domain proximity and sufficient pretraining scale, especially for CT-based models with broad data availability. Significance: These results demonstrate that both domain proximity and dataset scale jointly determine the effectiveness of self-supervised pretraining. While higher domain alignment improves performance at comparable scale, sufficient data is required to realize this benefit. CT-based pretraining provides a favorable balance between domain relevance and data availability, leading to robust performance across tasks. This study provides practical guidance for selecting pretraining strategies in PET/CT segmentation.
evidence_items.title: Domain-aligned self-supervision: CT-specialized DINOv3 enhances PET/CT tumor segmentation.

evidence_items.summary: Ecotourism promotes sustainable development, but evaluating tourists’ experiences becomes difficult because of different multi-source feedback. Traditional methods using text or rating have been inaccurate. Research incorporates textual reviews and numerical ratings to enhance precision, depth and interpretability in ecotourism sentiments and satisfaction evaluation. The primary goal is to develop and validate an intelligent multi-source framework capable of robust sentiment classification and satisfaction prediction. To achieve this, this research proposes a Green Anaconda Optimized Long Short-Term Transformer Memory (GAO-LSTR) model that integrates the established LSTM–Transformer hybrid model with Green Anaconda Optimization (GAO) to improve parameter optimization, contextual feature learning, and multi-source sentiment classification performance. Multi-source data is gathered from ecotourism platforms, online review systems, and social media sources, including the Ecotourism Sentiment and Satisfaction Dataset. Text preprocessing includes tokenization and stop-word removal. TF-IDF is used for textual feature vectorization, while BERT is utilized to generate contextualized semantic embeddings from textual reviews, capturing deep linguistic and contextual relationships for improved feature representation. Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) layers capture sequential linguistic patterns, and Transformer components model long-range dependencies. The GAO is employed to optimize the hyperparameters of the LSTR, while network weights are learned through Adam-based backpropagation, thereby improving convergence stability, robustness, and predictive performance. The framework is implemented in Python using TensorFlow and PyTorch. On the benchmark Ecotourism Sentiment and Satisfaction Dataset containing structured sentiment annotations, the proposed GAO-LSTR model achieved an accuracy of 98.13% for sentiment classification and 79% for the satisfaction prediction task. The combined usage of textual and numerical characteristics guarantees high robustness, better interpretability, and consistently high prediction quality. The framework significantly enhances ecotourism sentiment and satisfaction evaluation by effectively integrating heterogeneous data modalities. The GAO-LSTR model provides a scalable and reliable solution for real-world ecotourism analytics, supporting improved decision-making and promoting sustainable tourism development. The GAO-LSTR model combines LSTM and Transformer to accurately analyze the sentiment in ecotourism using multiple sources. TF-IDF and BERT embeddings are used to identify important features from the text data. The model performs very well with accuracy of 98. 13% and F-measure of 97.8%, surpassing unimodal models. Framework provides an efficient, meaningful, and practical evaluation of tourists’ sentiments and satisfaction. The GAO-LSTR model combines LSTM and Transformer to accurately analyze the sentiment in ecotourism using multiple sources. TF-IDF and BERT embeddings are used to identify important features from the text data. The model performs very well with accuracy of 98. 13% and F-measure of 97.8%, surpassing unimodal models. Framework provides an efficient, meaningful, and practical evaluation of tourists’ sentiments and satisfaction.
evidence_items.title: Sentiment analysis and satisfaction evaluation of ecotourism consumption under a multi-source deep learning framework

evidence_items.summary:
Background
Standardized metrics such as the numeric rating scale (NRS) provide essential quantitative pain benchmarks but can be augmented by capturing the functional and emotional context of a patient's lived experience. Adding surveys creates a "contextual disconnect" (increasing data yield with diminishing insights) and adds patient burden. The CONNECT (Collecting Communication Data to Enhance Patient-Physician Interaction) study proposes a structured, multimodal framework integrating patient narratives, drawings, and mobility assessments to capture each patient's holistic "pain story" and create a comprehensive ground truth dataset for developing digital health tools.


Objective
This study aims to (1) evaluate the feasibility of capturing multimodal communication data (narratives, drawings, and mobility) from patients with chronic pain, (2) quantify gaps between standard clinical metrics (eg, the NRS) and patient-defined key functional limitations, and (3) evaluate the usability and perceived communication value of software prototypes (myStory).


Methods
CONNECT is a multiphase, multicenter, exploratory feasibility study using human-centered design. Up to 3 tertiary care interventional pain practices in the United States will enroll 2 mutually exclusive cohorts (up to 40 patients each). Phase 1 conceptualizes the patient narrative as a "clinical sensor," collecting a foundational ground truth dataset via video-recorded pain narratives, guided drawings, standardized mobility assessments, and validated surveys. Phase 2 uses phase 1 learnings to develop and evaluate up to 5 myStory prototypes, assessing utility, usability, and perceived communication value via task-based evaluation and think-aloud protocols. Exploratory analyses include dual-coder thematic analysis, pose estimation mobility assessments, and AI-assisted narrative summarization.


Results
Recruitment began in May 2026. As of September 2026, one site is active, with 37 participants enrolled. Anticipated outcomes include (1) a rich, multimodal dataset establishing a ground truth of patient-derived functional limitations, goals, and expectations; (2) characterization of pain story gaps missed by the NRS via the contextual disconnect rate (defined as NRS ≤6 with ≥1 key functional limitation); (3) evaluation of at least one feasible prototype concept (mean score of 3.0 on a 5-point Likert scale); and (4) initial user testing of new communication assessment scales. Results are anticipated in late 2026 and will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications and conferences.


Conclusions
This protocol establishes a reproducible framework for understanding the holistic "pain story" by capturing narrative, visual, and functional dimensions of chronic pain. Findings will inform new communication tools intended to enhance patient-provider communication and align care with outcomes that matter most to patients with chronic pain.
evidence_items.title: A Human-Centered Framework to Capture the Holistic Pain Story in Chronic Pain: Protocol for a Multicenter Observational Feasibility Study.

evidence_items.summary: DNA motif discovery and, particularly, computational modeling of transcription factor binding motifs, has been a mecca of algorithmic bioinformatics for several decades. Here, we report the results of the largest open community challenge in Inferring BInding Specificities (IBIS), where participants all over the world were invited to construct binding specificity models from multi-assay experimental data for poorly studied human transcription factors. The submissions were rigorously tested against a rich held-out dataset. Benchmarking demonstrated a consistent advantage of properly designed deep learning models over traditional positional weight matrices and other machine learning methods. Yet, the positional weight matrices displayed a surprisingly strong performance out of the box, being only slightly behind the best deep learning models. A post-challenge assessment of a selection of other deep learning methods further solidified this finding. IBIS highlights the power of benchmarking in finding adequate DNA motif representations, emphasizes the pros and cons of various machine learning methods applied to DNA motif modeling, and establishes a rich dataset, benchmarking protocols, and computational framework for a fair cross-platform evaluation of future models of transcription factor binding motifs in DNA sequences.
evidence_items.title: Inferring binding specificities of human transcription factors with the wisdom of crowds.

evidence_items.summary: Explainability is an important requirement for machine learning models in high-risk domains such as medicine. We introduce HierViT, a hierarchical Vision Transformer that combines competitive predictive performance with multiple mechanisms to support the interpretation of its predictions. The model first predicts clinically relevant visual appearance attributes, which are then used to infer the final target prediction through a hierarchical reasoning process. To facilitate understanding of the intermediate representations, attribute-specific prototypes are visualized as representative image examples, while attribute-specific attention maps highlight image regions associated with each visual feature. Together, these attribute-level components provide complementary views of the model's reasoning by linking representative image examples and spatial attention to semantically defined visual features. We evaluate HierViT on two medical benchmark datasets: LIDC-IDRI for lung nodule assessment and derm7pt for skin lesion classification. Across both datasets, HierViT achieves competitive predictive performance while providing attribute-level prototypes and attention visualizations that support the interpretation of its predictions.
evidence_items.title: Hierarchical Vision Transformer with Prototypes for Interpretable Medical Image Classification.

evidence_items.summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/23293074 . Thank you for this paper. You take TRACE's public corpus of 590 harness-triggered compaction boundaries on AppWorld, each replayed under the pre-compaction context (PRE) and under the summary (POST), and ask whether what the agent did before a boundary predicts the burden of its next actions - calls that error or repeat a call already made (Sections 1-2). The placement contrast is a wide null, and the "has-written" label mostly tracks trajectory phase (Section 3). The best extension trigger reaches held-out AUROC 0.66 against 0.72 for a same-boundary replicate (Section 4). I liked that Appendix A dates every amendment and reports the gates that were not met. I read it as a practitioner who runs coding agents every day. In my company the software development is done by AI agents, so maybe my practical side is useful here. Four comments. 1. On what a blocked compaction costs - The frontier counts compaction opportunities with equal weight, because the release has no token counts (Section 4, Appendix A), and the offline value prices only the next k actions (Section 5). For me the other side of this trade is the bill. In my own logs (722 sessions, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22759216) more than 85% of the modeled cost was work with context (cache reads plus cache writes), and sessions longer than 200 calls (8% of sessions) gave more than 90% of the money. The cost is modeled from a price list, not from invoices. So a blocked compaction has a price too - the PRE context stays in every later call. When corpora ship token counts, could the x-axis weight each opportunity by the tokens a compaction would remove? That would also allow the token-budget comparison that the abstract says cannot be evaluated on this release. 2.
evidence_items.title: PREreview of "Does an Agent's History Tell You When Compaction Will Hurt? A Modest, Bounded Effect on the TRACE Paired-Replay Corpus"

evidence_items.summary: Version 2.0. Reproducibility package for a field study of automated in-hive Varroa destructor surveillance. Cite the concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23099411, which always resolves to the latest version. The code and the small data files are also browsable at https://github.com/Soda0603/varroa-in-hive-imaging. CONTENTS 2,823 annotated RGB images with YOLO-format bounding boxes, in two parts that must be reported separately: 2,795 frames captured inside an active Apis mellifera colony by a motorised sliding-rail camera (Raspberry Pi Camera Module V2, 1920 x 1080), and 28 handheld close-range photographs added to increase the number of mite examples. Two classes: Bee without visible mite (0) and Bee with visible mite (1). 4,692 class-0 and 87 class-1 boxes. The label marks the bee, not the mite. Also included: five-fold stratified split definitions (seed 42), training configurations and trained best.pt weights for eight architectures (YOLOv7, YOLOv8n, YOLOv9c, YOLOv10n, YOLO11n, YOLO12n, YOLOv13n, YOLO26n), the evaluation code behind the published tables, a mite-level annotation layer, and a per-annotation verification record. ACQUISITION The platform operated from 8 December 2023 to 8 March 2024 (92 days) at Chenhome Apiary, Fangshan Township, Pingtung County, Taiwan, recording 22,442 frames at a nominal six-minute interval. 19,619 (87.4%) were discarded as motion-blurred. The retained in-hive frames carry timestamps on nine capture days, so the annotated set is a sparse sample of the deployment rather than a uniform one. MITE-LEVEL RE-INSPECTION Every class-1 annotation was re-inspected at mite level by an author with five years of research experience with the species. 56 of 87 were confirmed: 53 of 64 in the supplementary photographs, but only 3 of 23 in the in-hive frames. The re-inspection also produced 69 tight mite boxes as a separate layer, of which 36 mark mites the original annotation had missed. The original labels are unchanged.
evidence_items.title: In-hive Varroa destructor imaging: dataset, mite-level re-inspection layer, cross-validation splits, evaluation code and model weights

evidence_items.summary: Paired benchmark of local language model generation speed on one HP Notebook (Intel Core i3-5005U, 2 cores / 4 threads, 6 GB RAM, Intel HD Graphics 5500). The laptop was tested under Windows 10 Home 22H2 (build 19045) on 2026-09-29, then under Linux Mint 22.3 "Zena" (Cinnamon 6.6.4, kernel 6.14.0-37-generic) on 2026-10-10. Both runs used Ollama 0.11.4 and the same tinyllama Q4 0 model (digest 2644915ede352ea7bdfaff0bfac0be74c719d5d5202acb63a6fb095b52f394a4), CPU-only (num gpu: 0), temperature 0, seed 42 and num predict 200: one cold request after unloading the model, then three warm requests. Results: median warm generation throughput was 12.9 tokens/s on Linux Mint and 9.4 tokens/s on Windows 10 (+37.2%, ratio 1.37). Cold full-answer completion took 19.8 s on Mint and 229.8 s on Windows; the Windows figure includes about 167 s of Ollama runner startup. Ollama reported 0.7 GB of loaded model memory on both systems. Limitations: this is a paired whole-system comparison and does not isolate the operating system as the cause. Windows had desktop applications and the Ollama tray app running; background activity and the power profile on Mint during inference were not recorded. Each system has three warm runs from a single session, and individual run rates were not retained, so variability cannot be estimated. Files: linux-mint-report-20261010.md (method, results, calculations and limitations); windows.csv and linux-mint-cinnamon-20261010-144025.csv (aggregate results per operating system); bench.py (the benchmark script, unmodified, from repository commit 491c71a).
evidence_items.title: CPU-only local LLM benchmark on an HP Notebook (Intel Core i3-5005U): Linux Mint 22.3 vs Windows 10, Ollama 0.11.4, TinyLlama Q4_0

evidence_items.summary: This study aimed to determine the optimum level of maltodextrin incorporation as a bulking agent in the production of mango fruit bars and to evaluate their physical properties, sensory acceptability, proximate composition, and vitamin C content. Mangoes were processed through washing, peeling, deseeding, depulping, and pureeing, followed by the incorporation of maltodextrin at 1%, 3%, and 5% (w/w), with a control formulation containing no maltodextrin. The mixtures were adjusted to 25°Brix total soluble solids (TSS), heated, sulfited, dried at 55°C for 17 hours, molded, and packaged. The physical properties of the fruit bars were evaluated by measuring thickness, while sensory acceptability was determined using a 9-point Hedonic Scale with 25 panelists. The optimum formulation was further analyzed for proximate composition and vitamin C content and compared with the control. Results showed that increasing the maltodextrin concentration significantly increased the thickness of the mango fruit bars, with the 3% and 5% formulations producing thicknesses of 9.38 mm and 10.63 mm, respectively. Sensory evaluation revealed that the formulation containing 3% maltodextrin obtained the highest acceptability scores, particularly for texture, flavor, and overall acceptability. Proximate  composition analysis further demonstrated that the 3% maltodextrin formulation contained significantly higher ash (1.455%), protein (2.495%), total dietary fiber (3.775%), and vitamin C (40.350 mg/100 g) than the control ( p < 0.05), while moisture and carbohydrate contents were comparable between formulations. Although the control exhibited a slightly higher fat content, both formulations remained low in fat. These findings indicate that the incorporation of 3% maltodextrin improved nutrient retention and enhanced the nutritional quality of the mango fruit bars without compromising their desirable physical characteristics.
evidence_items.title: Optimization of maltodextrin as a bulking agent in mango (Mangifera indica) fruit bar: Physical, sensory, and nutritional evaluation

evidence_items.summary: The protection of space assets has become a critical concern, as the intelligence and communication capabilities they provide are essential in an environment where threats must now be considered in orbit itself. Ground-based observation remains the conventional approach for detecting potential hazards, such as conjunctions or uncooperative close-approach events, with avoidance manoeuvres subsequently commanded from ground control. Space-based space surveillance offers a complementary alternative: it provides higher-quality imagery and, when combined with on-board processing, enables significantly shorter response times. On-board detection, however, imposes a substantial computational load, as 4k×4k images constitute the operational standard. Furthermore, robust tracking of Resident Space Objects (RSOs) favours the direct processing of image sequences rather than single frames, which further increases the computational burden. Finally, since real space-to-space imagery remains scarce, a simulator generating RSO image sequences is required to train deep learning models on a sufficient number of samples covering the diversity of acquisition conditions. Within these constraints, this paper presents the complete processing chain of our solution, from image modelling to on-board evaluation on synthetic data. A key result is a deep neural network deployed on an AMD Versal Edge development kit achieving a throughput of 130 Mpix/s while maintaining a F1 score of 87%. This performance allows five 4k×4k images to be processed in under one second, meeting real-time acquisition requirements.
evidence_items.title: On the detection of RSO on board using AI

evidence_items.summary: ABSTRACT This study evaluates the predictive limits of machine learning architectures within highly volatile digital asset regimes by forecasting stationary log returns rather than non-stationary raw price levels. To bypass standard look-ahead bias and identity function vulnerabilities common in applied financial machine learning, we construct a forecasting engine utilizing five years of daily historical Ethereum (ETH-USD) market metrics spanning January 1, 2021, to December 31, 2025. Given that Ethereum's real-world all-time high occurred historically in November 2021, metrics generated during the 2025 out-of-sample window are formally treated as part of a simulated evaluation framework to test model performance limits under high market noise. Descriptive statistical analysis identified an absolute absence of a linear relationship (correlation coefficient of -0.01) between daily log trading volume and asset returns. A Random Forest Regressor was trained on a chronological data split (2021–2024) and evaluated against an out-of-sample testing window spanning the full year of 2025. Benchmarked against a 7-Day Simple Moving Average (SMA), empirical results demonstrated that the baseline 7-Day SMA achieved a superior Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.029914, outperforming the Random Forest model's error of 0.031403. A formal Diebold-Mariano statistical significance test yielded a test statistic of -0.9383 with a corresponding p-value of 0.3481. Because the p-value sits significantly above the standard academic threshold of 0.05, the null hypothesis of equal predictive accuracy cannot be rejected. These findings present a valuable academic null result, proving that when forced to forecast true stationary daily log returns, classical rolling statistical benchmarks can systematically out-predict complex non-linear machine learning architectures.
evidence_items.title: EMPIRICAL EVALUATION OF TREE-BASED MACHINE LEARNING MODEL AGAINST SIMPLE MOVING AVERAGE IN CRYPTO ASSET FORECASTING

evidence_items.summary: Supporting data and code for the paper "Does the Router Know? Mixture-of-Experts Routing Signals for Detecting Silent Errors in Text-to-SQL over University Data Warehouses" (submitted to Knowledge-Based Systems, Elsevier). An agentic assistant built on the open-weight Mixture-of-Experts model gpt-oss-120b answers questions in Italian over the live data warehouse of a public university, on premises and without a GPU. Its most damaging failures are silent: a query that runs, returns a plausible number, and answers a different question from the one asked. This deposit contains: a benchmark of 1000 Italian questions from 51 templates, with reference values verified against the institution's own reports and the date each value was read; the error labels for three system configurations, together with the human review behind them and the stratified sample used to validate the references; the assistant's answers as returned; per-layer router statistics for all 36 layers of the model, extracted post hoc by replaying each answer through a teacher-forced forward pass in llama.cpp and capturing the router tensors, validated against the experts the model actually selected; the reports produced by the probes, including AUROC by feature family, control tasks and risk-coverage curves; the semantic layer, that is the official measure behind each institutional report and the catalogue of the 283 warehouse tables; and all the code, from routing extraction to probe evaluation. All material is aggregated. No person-level data was processed or released at any stage. The internal page and API addresses of the institutional dashboard have been removed from two files, which keep the measure definitions and default filters relied on by the paper. Data, labels and documentation are released under CC BY 4.0; the code is additionally available under the MIT licence. Access to the files is currently restricted and granted on request; it will be opened on publication of the article.
evidence_items.title: Routing signals for silent-error detection in text-to-SQL over a university data warehouse: benchmark, labels and code

evidence_items.summary: Groundwater serves as a vital resource for drinking and household needs across rural communities in Maharashtra's Chandrapur District. This research was conducted to examine the physicochemical properties of local groundwater and determine its viability for human consumption and daily use. Water samples gathered from various rural sites in the district underwent laboratory testing for key parameters using standard analytical methods, encompassing color, calcium, chloride, electrical conductivity, fluoride, magnesium, nitrate, pH, total dissolved solids, total alkalinity, total hardness, turbidity, iron, and sulfate, with results benchmarked against established drinking-water standards. Furthermore, the study highlights geographic variations in water quality driven by regional geology and human factors such as farming practices, domestic wastewater, and improper waste disposal. This evaluation pinpoints specific water parameters and locations requiring focused public water management, ultimately emphasizing the necessity of consistent monitoring, proper treatment, source safeguarding, and contamination control to preserve safe and sustainable groundwater supplies in rural Chandrapur.
evidence_items.title: Assessment of Ground Water Quality from Rural Areas of Chandrapur District, Maharashtra, India

evidence_items.summary: Background/Objectives: Automated visual inspection of pharmaceutical tablets is increasingly important for detecting manufacturing defects and maintaining consistent product quality. Progress in artificial intelligence-based defect classification is, however, constrained by the scarcity of publicly accessible image datasets covering defective tablets under diverse visual conditions. This study introduces the PharmaVision (PV) dataset, a public visual dataset and benchmark for classifying normal and defective compressed tablets. Methods: The PV dataset contains 640 smartphone-acquired images spanning varied tablet products, backgrounds, and lighting, with fixed tablet-level splits (190/190 training, 30/30 validation, and 100/100 test images for the normal and defective classes, respectively). Twelve representative architectures spanning classical convolutional networks, mobile networks, and vision transformers were benchmarked under an identical protocol using accuracy, precision, recall, and harmonic mean of precision and recall (F1-score), with 95% confidence intervals and paired statistical tests. Cross-dataset generalization was assessed on the independent pillQC dataset without fine-tuning, and efficiency was profiled using parameters, Giga floating-point operations (GFLOPs), latency, and throughput. Results: EfficientNetV2-S achieved the highest F1-score on the PV test set (88.56%), although paired statistical tests did not distinguish it from Xception (87.08%) or Swin-B (85.71%). On pillQC, GoogLeNet and EfficientNetV2-S showed the strongest cross-dataset performance, whereas both vision transformers declined relative to their in-domain results. AlexNet gave the highest theoretical throughput (602.41 frames per second (FPS), median latency 1.66 ms), whereas ShuffleNetV2 and MobileNetV3-small offered the smallest parameter counts.
evidence_items.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Quality Control of Pharmaceutical Tablets: A Visual Dataset and Benchmark for Automated Defect Detection

StrengthSense offers a benchmark for studying cross-subject recognition, sensor placement, reduced-sensor deployment, sensing-modality contribution, and physical-function monitoring. evidence_items.summary: This repository benchmarks 11 AI models on a task customs brokers do every day: assigning the tariff code (HTS) to a product from its description alone. The ground truth is 1,098 binding rulings issued by US Customs and Border Protection (CBP CROSS, New York) between January and August 2026, with duty rates taken from the USITC tariff schedule. Models range from small free ones to Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Sol. Every model is graded on the same 228 rulings dated after the latest training cutoff among them (July to mid-August 2026), so no model is compared on easier or possibly memorised material. A second table uses all 1,098 rulings as an upper bound. Main findings: (1) Even the best models get the 8-digit code that sets the duty right only about half the time (Claude Opus 5.5 53.5%, GPT-6 Sol 49.1% on the same 228; the two are statistically tied). (2) The small free models score under 6%. (3) The best models’ errors are mostly real codes for the wrong product, so a “does this code exist?” check catches only about a third of them. (4) When a wrong code changes the duty, most models lean toward underpaying (7 of 11 beat a chance baseline); Claude Opus 5.5 does not show it. Dollar figures use base (MFN) duty only, so they are a minimum. Limits: base duty only (no Section 301 or 232), New York rulings only, models answer from the description with no tariff lookup, four models have no stated training cutoff, and reasoning could not be switched off for some. Analysis plans were pre-registered and every deviation is logged. Includes the data, code, prompts, per-ruling model outputs and a script that verifies every number in the README.
evidence_items.title: Tariff Cost Benchmark: Duty-at-Stake and Direction Bias in LLM Customs Classification

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Large language models require reproducible outputs for systematic evaluation in tumor boards. We developed a sarcoma tumor-board simulator using Claude Opus 4.5 at temperature 0.0, schema-enforced JSON output, and prompt-specified semantic and conditional-logic rules. The framework was evaluated on 51 de-identified cases across 154 runs. Reproducibility was defined as agreement across all runs of a case per decision code. In the 41 cases not used during development, reproducibility was 94.2% (cluster-bootstrap 95% CI 91.9–96.1); in the 10 development cases, 93.3% (95% CI 88.6–97.6). Pooled, it was 94.0% (95% CI 92.0–95.8); 17 cases agreed on all 21 codes. Estimates are model-specific. A post hoc ablation on 15 cases compared the framework with and without these rules: 94.6% versus 82.5% (difference 12.1 points; 95% CI 7.6–17.1). The improvement was driven mainly by exact wording agreement in three free-text fields (+ 60.0 points), whereas the 18 categorical and numeric codes differed by 4.1 points (95% CI − 0.7 to 9.3). Without any schema, a decision was stated for only 37.6% of instances versus 100% under schema enforcement; seven codes were never addressed. Single-reviewer screening detected no fabricated numbers, references, or measurements. Clinical correctness was not assessed. Consistent recommendations may still be incorrect.
evidence_items.title: A schema-enforced large language model framework produces largely reproducible decision codes in simulated sarcoma tumor boards

evidence_items.summary: Reliable classification of transposable elements (TEs) is important for genome annotation and evolutionary analysis, yet remains challenging: TE families differ widely across taxa, reference databases label them inconsistently, and many TEs are represented only by degraded copies. We introduce GLARE (Genomic Language model for Automated Repetitive Element classification), a TE classifier built by fine-tuning a genomic language model on harmonized PanTEon and Repbase reference data to predict TE superfamily across 32 superfamilies in 11 orders. Among the genomic language models compared, Nucleotide Transformer v3 provided the strongest representation. Built on this backbone, GLARE exceeded all nine classifiers in the PanTEon benchmark, reaching 0.966 weighted superfamily F1 on its 30-superfamily task. GLARE also showed stronger generalization to clades absent from training, consistently exceeding state-of-the-art classifiers on holdouts spanning three taxonomic ranks: the order Poales, the phylum Arthropoda, and the kingdom Fungi. Training on both PanTEon and Repbase reduced the performance drop seen when a single-source model was applied to the other database. Under simulated sequence decay, GLARE was the most robust classifier tested, and it performed best on independently curated degraded libraries. These findings show that genomic language models fine-tuned on harmonized multi-source references can classify TEs robustly under the taxonomic, database, and sequence-quality shifts that matter in practice. GLARE is available at https://code.jgi.doe.gov/NHaas/glare.
evidence_items.title: GLARE: Genomic Language model for Automated Repetitive Element classification

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Patients considering robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP) require information that spans diagnosis, treatment selection, functional recovery, and recurrence surveillance. We compared the quality of English-language RARP patient education generated by ChatGPT, DeepSeek, and Doubao. Twenty-five questions covering screening, diagnosis, treatment decision-making, perioperative care, rehabilitation, and follow-up were submitted individually to each model, yielding 75 responses. Three blinded clinicians evaluated the responses using the Global Quality Score, modified DISCERN, Quality Analysis of Medical Artificial Intelligence, Ensuring Quality Information for Patients, and the Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool; six readability indices were also calculated. Overall Global Quality Scores did not differ significantly across models. ChatGPT achieved a higher EQIP score (median, 75.00%) than DeepSeek and Doubao (65.83% each) and greater PEMAT actionability (59.00% vs. 54.33% and 47.67%, respectively). DeepSeek generated comparatively easier-to-read text, although all three models exceeded commonly recommended sixth- to eighth-grade reading levels for public-facing health materials. Under the majority-rater criterion, no factual errors or outdated recommendations were identified, whereas key omissions occurred mainly in DeepSeek and Doubao responses. Inter-rater agreement was low, indicating substantial uncertainty in multidimensional human assessment. LLMs may support the preparation of clinician-reviewed RARP educational materials but should not replace individualized counseling by urologists.
evidence_items.title: Large language models differ in patient education quality across the robot-assisted radical prostatectomy care pathway

evidence_items.summary: Large language models are increasingly part of how people seek support and communicate with others, while also reproducing normative assumptions about how people think, interact, and express themselves. This dissertation investigates how these assumptions surface for neurodivergent people across individual and interpersonal contexts. My preliminary work examined how neurodivergent adults use LLMs for communication and emotional support, finding that responses often missed users’ thought processes, communication styles, and support needs. Building on this work, I am developing a dataset of 150 dyadic conversations, with utterance-level annotations and written rationales from both autistic and neurotypical participants. I use these annotations to examine how understanding, misunderstanding, and repair unfold across dyads, and to evaluate whether LLM interpretations of the same moments align more closely with autistic or neurotypical participants’ perspectives. This dissertation contributes empirical evidence and participant-grounded methods for examining the normative assumptions embedded in AI systems that shape interpersonal communication.
evidence_items.title: Neurotypical Assumptions in Large Language Models Across Individual Support and Interpersonal Communication

organizations: University of Copenhagen
evidence_items.summary: Direct RNA nanopore sequencing offers the capacity to directly profile native RNAs, enabling detection of diverse epitranscriptomic modifications based on current changes as the RNA passes through a pore. Innovations in chemistry, hardware and bioinformatic tools have increased sequencing capacity and accuracy, creating demand for sequencing multiple samples within individual runs. Two recent solutions enable barcoding and demultiplexing of samples, but independent comparisons of their performance is limited. Here we benchmark WarpDemuX and SeqTagger using orthogonal ground truths derived from species identity and matched IVT spike-ins across four RNA004 flow cells. Both achieve high demultiplexing precision but differ in their trade-offs in precision and retention. SeqTagger provided strong performance at its recommended settings, whilst WarpDemuX performance varied by model, barcode and read quality. IVT-derived score cutoffs allowed dataset-specific calibration and increased WarpDeMux assignment yield, although precision achieved on IVTs was not consistently reproduced in species reads. These results support matched IVTs as internal controls for guiding choice of demultiplexing settings, while demonstrating the need to validate demultiplexing precision in biological RNA populations.
evidence_items.title: Systematic benchmark of demultiplexing workflows for direct RNA sequencing

evidence_items.summary: Objective: The objective of this study was to evaluate the diagnostic performance of GPT-5.2 Thinking in identifying oral potentially malignant disorders within a patient sample that also included oral carcinomas and other oral cavity lesions, using intraoral photographs and associated clinical data. Methods: This retrospective exploratory diagnostic accuracy study included 103 oral lesions: 69 oral potentially malignant disorders, 25 oral carcinomas, and 9 other oral pathologies. Each case was assessed in three independent sessions, and the majority diagnosis was compared with the final clinical and/or histopathological reference diagnosis. Results: For oral potentially malignant disorders, sensitivity was 92.75%, specificity was 88.24%, accuracy was 91.26%, positive predictive value was 94.12%, negative predictive value was 85.71%, and Cohen’s kappa was 0.804. Sensitivity was 81.82% for homogeneous leukoplakia, 78.57% for non-homogeneous leukoplakia, and 86.36% for oral lichen planus. For oral carcinomas, sensitivity was 84.00%, specificity was 97.44%, accuracy was 94.17%, positive predictive value was 91.30%, negative predictive value was 95.00%, and Cohen’s kappa was 0.837. Conclusions: GPT-5.2 Thinking showed promising diagnostic performance in this exploratory case-enriched dataset, but predictive values require validation in representative clinical populations.

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Motivation Systems biology strives to unravel the complex dynamics of cellular processes using ordinary differential equations. However, the sparsity of measured data and the strong non-linearity of common ordinary differential equations introduce severe numerical problems in modeling tasks. This motivated the development of computational algorithms that must be systematically evaluated to ensure optimal method choices. The amount of well-curated models for such benchmarking efforts is insufficient, as building and calibrating biologically reasonable models from experiments requires years of work. Results We present a large-scale collection of 1100 synthetic modeling problems, generated based on the systems of ordinary differential equations and experimental designs of 22 published modeling problems. This is achieved by extending a recent method for simulation of time-course data for randomly generated observation functions to also include realistic measurement patterns across multiple experimental conditions. By analyzing data and model characteristics, optimization performance and parameter identifiability, we show that the synthetic problems provide both a realistic and diverse extension of the existing problem space. Hence, the synthetic collection provides a valuable resource for benchmarking in dynamic modeling. Availability and Implementation Benchmark problems and algorithm are publicly available at https://github.com/niklasneubrand/1100SyntheticBenchmarksODE and https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23211070.
evidence_items.title: 1100 Synthetic Benchmark Problems for Dynamic Modeling of Cellular Processes
