evidence_items.summary:
RATIONALE
Patients who use alcohol as a sleep aid may experience withdrawal-related insomnia and hyperarousal, which can reinforce continued drinking. Bionic sleep therapy (BST) is an exploratory intervention using intravenous anesthetic and sedative agents under close monitoring to induce a brief, controllable, sleep-like state. It may provide short-term support for sleep initiation during early alcohol withdrawal.


PATIENT CONCERNS
A 71-year-old man had chronic insomnia for over 15 years and consumed 100 to 200 mL of Chinese baijiu nightly to initiate sleep, with additional alcohol after nocturnal awakenings. Repeated attempts to stop drinking were followed by worsening insomnia, restlessness, palpitations, diaphoresis, and intense alcohol craving, which improved after drinking.


DIAGNOSES
Chronic insomnia with recurrent mild alcohol withdrawal-related symptoms and a high risk of complicated alcohol withdrawal.


INTERVENTIONS
The patient underwent 2 monitored BST sessions on hospital days 1 and 2 under continuous cardiorespiratory monitoring. Propofol (1 mg/kg) was administered intravenously for rapid induction, followed by a 60-minute dexmedetomidine infusion via an IV pump at 0.2 to 0.4 μg/kg/h. Multimodal treatment was intensified on hospital day 2, including cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia, medication adjustment, and adjunctive neuromodulation.


OUTCOMES
During the overall multimodal treatment course, on the night of the first BST session, the patient initiated sleep without alcohol and returned to sleep after a nocturnal awakening without further drinking. Polysomnography showed a total sleep time of 373 minutes and sleep efficiency of 85.6%. Following the second session, he consumed approximately 20 mL of alcohol after a nocturnal awakening before returning to sleep; sleep diary-reported sleep efficiency was 90.6%. Vital signs remained stable during both sessions, and no apparent anesthesia- or sedation-related adverse events occurred. No further alcohol intake was recorded from hospital day 3 to day 7. At discharge, subjective sleep efficiency was 87.7%, with improvements in sleep initiation, maintenance, and some daytime symptoms. Postdischarge follow-up data were unavailable.


LESSONS
BST using propofol and dexmedetomidine may warrant further investigation as an adjunct to multimodal management in patients with chronic insomnia, long-term alcohol use as a sleep aid, and withdrawal-related symptoms. However, improvements cannot be attributed specifically to BST, and its contribution and durability require prospective evaluation.
evidence_items.title: Bionic sleep therapy combined with multimodal management for chronic insomnia with alcohol withdrawal-related symptoms: A case report.

evidence_items.summary:
In Indigenous communities where governance integrates land, ancestors and more-than-human beings, standardised risk assessments overlooking relational ontologies may produce incomplete evaluations and inadvertently deepen vulnerabilities. This article analyses ontological frictions in disaster risk assessment (DRA) arising from the encounter between standardised frameworks and Indigenous relational ontologies enacted through governance systems.
 
 
 
 Six weeks of ethnographic fieldwork in Yaqui communities of Sonora, Mexico, including interviews (n = 35), focus groups (n = 5), participant observation, participatory mapping and archival review. Analysis identified instances where positivist risk categories encountered limits when engaging with Yaqui conceptions of territory, causality and agency.
 
 
 
 Three ontological frictions emerged: (1) spatial segmentation conflicts with territory as an integral entity structured by lu'uturia yo'owe, a Yaqui cosmogonic governance principle; (2) framing phenomena as climate exposure abstracts political agents into environmental factors, depoliticising territorial conflict and dissolving relational accountability; (3) analytical translation recasts governance-constitutive entities as cultural descriptors, obscuring their organising role and rendering governance invisible to assessment instruments.
 
 
 
 Where relational ordering prevails, the absence of recognisable administrative infrastructure requires consideration of other sources of such infrastructure. Meaningful engagement therefore requires interrogating the ontological assumptions embedded in assessment tools, not just enhancing culturally sensitive consultation.
 
 
 
 This article empirically demonstrates how ontological frictions permeate DRA processes and advances the concept of instrument deficit as an analytical lens for risk governance in Indigenous contexts shaped by climate and territorial pressures.
evidence_items.title: Ontological frictions in disaster risk assessment: evidence from Yaqui territories, Mexico

evidence_items.summary: Introduction: Cystic fibrosis is an autosomal recessive disease caused by mutations in the CFTR gene, leading to impaired ion transport, thickening of secretions, and damage to the bronchopulmonary system. Progressive mucoobstruction remains the leading cause of mortality. To improve sputum rheological properties, mucolytics (dornase alfa) and rehydrating agents (hypertonic saline, mannitol) are used; however, their role in the era of highly effective targeted therapy remains debatable. Aim: To evaluate the relationship between nutritional status, the regimen of mucoactive therapy, and pulmonary ventilation function parameters in children with cystic fibrosis receiving targeted therapy. Materials and methods: A single-center cross-sectional study was conducted involving 50 patients (aged 6–17 years) with cystic fibrosis receiving elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor. Spirometry parameters (FEV1, FVC), nutritional status (BAZ), and the inhalation therapy regimen (dornase alfa, hypertonic saline) were analyzed. Results: The study included 24 (48%) boys and 26 (52%) girls, with a mean patient age of 12.5±3.1 years. A statistically significant positive correlation was found between BAZ and FEV1 (Rs=0.432; p=0.002) and FVC (Rs=0.450; p=0.001). Patients receiving combined mucoactive therapy (dornase alfa + hypertonic saline) had significantly higher FEV1 values compared to the dornase alfa monotherapy group (p=0.027). The frequency of administration of each drug individually did not correlate significantly with functional parameters (p > 0.05). Conclusion: Nutritional status is closely associated with lung function in children with cystic fibrosis. Combined mucoactive therapy is associated with a clinically significant improvement in bronchial patency even in the context of targeted treatment, which justifies maintaining mucolytic therapy in the comprehensive management of patients. Prospective randomized studies are required to definitively confirm the benefit of the combination.
evidence_items.title: ASSOCIATION OF NUTRITIONAL STATUS AND MUCOACTIVE THERAPY REGIMEN WITH LUNG FUNCTION PARAMETERS IN CHILDREN WITH CYSTIC FIBROSIS AGED 6–17 YEARS RECEIVING ELEXACAFTOR/TEZACAFTOR/IVACAFTOR: A CROSS-SECTIONAL STUDY

evidence_items.summary:
BACKGROUND & AIMS
Recurrence of hepatocellular carcinoma (r-HCC) remains a major determinant of post-transplant (LT) outcomes. The 2024 ILTS-ILCA consensus highlighted the need for contemporary data assessing how evolving selection criteria and therapeutic strategies over the past 15 years have influenced prognosis.


METHODS
We conducted a retrospective study including all patients diagnosed with r-HCC following LT between 2008 and 2020 across 15 French transplant centres. Recurrence patterns, post-recurrence survival, and overall transplant outcomes were analysed, including temporal trends and the impact of AFP model implementation in 2013.


RESULTS
We analysed 388 patients with r-HCC, median time to recurrence was 19.1 months, with 26.3% occurring beyond 3 years. Earlier recurrence was associated with tumour-related factors (AFP and Milan criteria, αFP kinetics), and later recurrence with patient-related factors (HCV recurrence, alcohol relapse, grade 2 obesity). Following AFP model implementation, time to recurrence shortened (p<0.001). Surgical/ablative treatments improved survival in r-HCC in a subgroup of patients with single organ involvement of liver, lung or lymph nodes. Survival did not improve between patients diagnosed before 2016, between 2016 and 2018, or after 2018 (p=0.09). Calcineurin inhibitors or mycophenolate mofetil had no impact on survival, whereas mTOR inhibitor use was associated with significantly longer survival (20.7 vs 13.2 months, p=0.001).


CONCLUSIONS
r-HCC is a heterogeneous disease distinct from HCC in non-transplanted patients. Earlier recurrences following extended selection criteria implementation warrant caution. Surgical/ablative approaches should be prioritized even for extrahepatic disease. Despite expanded TKI options since 2016, outcomes of systemic treatment did not show statistical improvement. Post-recurrence mTOR inhibitors should be evaluated in clinical trials.


IMPACT AND IMPLICATIONS
This nationwide cohort study provides updated data on recurrence of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) after liver transplantation in the modern era, a special population excluded from major HCC trials, highlighting major heterogeneity in patients' trajectories before and after recurrence, variations across eras of selection criteria and systemic therapies, and an urgent unmet need as the approval of second-generation TKIs after 2016 did not incrementally improve survival. The study results are important for transplant hepatologists and liver oncologists to optimize patient selection for liver transplantation, to individualize prolongation of surveillance beyond the current ILTS-ILCA 3-year window recommendation based on patient-related risk factors for late recurrences, and prioritize radical treatments with curative intent for selected patients with single organ involvement of liver, lungs or lymph nodes, rather than a blanket systemic-only approach. The retrospective design of the analysis does not allow for formal demonstration of superiority of therapeutic strategies, but provide evidence to design clinical trials on newer systemic agents such as immune-checkpoint inhibitors.
